rv.q: Abrahami and her cast bring subtle shades of light and dark to these well-worn characters, underlining the sadness as well as the comedy of Leigh's suburbia.
The cast confidently wrings out all the requisite laughs and delivers on the stilted rhythms of every pregnant pause and awkward silence in Leigh's still painfully sharp and sparkling dialogue.
In this instance there is certainly enough theatrical gin in the glass to make for a highly entertaining party...
Abrahami’s production of Abigail’s Party is fantastic.
Abigail’s Party remains a classic and this run has been extended due to popular demand.
Overall this play was interesting and funny at times, yet not without its faults.
It’s so good you’ll want to book a second time and go and ‘party’ with Beverly again!
This beautifully designed production is a sensuous experience that forces the audience to look inwards at ourselves.
It's well acted, looks great, and there are definitely moments that made me laugh – especially anything Kym Marsh was doing.

cn.t: Critics praise this imaginative revival of Mike Leigh's classic, highlighting Natalie Abrahami's fresh direction and the Royal Exchange's immersive staging that brilliantly captures the boozy claustrophobia and dark comedy of suburban aspiration.
